input.question: Why aren't high rise office fires more common/unsurvivable?
input.ground_truth: They used to, then builders got wise to it. Now we build high rises out of concrete and glass, which don't catch on fire. We restrict how much flammable material is used on the floors of high rises and don't allow anything flammable at all in the stairwells (that's why the stairs are pretty much always barren concrete with metal railings), which makes it more difficult for the fires to spread between floors.

response.prediction: High-rise office fires are not as common or as deadly as they might seem because modern buildings are designed with strict fire safety regulations. These include the use of fire-resistant materials, multiple exit routes, clearly marked stairwells, automatic sprinkler systems, and advanced fire alarms. Buildings also undergo regular safety inspections and drills to ensure everyone knows what to do in an emergency. Because of these precautions, most high-rise fires are contained quickly, and people have enough time to evacuate safely. That’s why, even though high-rise fires can happen, they are rarely “unsurvivable” when the safety measures are followed.
